findings.title: DELETE /admin/users/<id> lacks the admin role check its sibling enforces
findings.description: delete_user is an admin route guarded only by login_required, while the adjacent promote_user also applies require_role("admin"). The OpenAPI spec additionally declares this DELETE with security: [].
findings.attack_scenario: A regular user issues DELETE /admin/users/<id> and the account row is deleted. (Not executed.)
findings.expected_boundary: Only administrators can delete users.
findings.observed_behavior: Any authenticated user passes the only guard.
findings.technical_impact: Unauthorized deletion of arbitrary user accounts (integrity/availability).

verification.rationale: delete_user carries only @login_required while promote_user adds @require_role('admin'); no global role check exists.

findings.safe_validation: Static comparison of decorators; confirm no global before_request role check exists.
findings.remediation: Add @require_role("admin") to delete_user and a regression test asserting 403 for non-admins.

Invoice ids are guessable integers (route uses <int:invoice_id>)
findings.title: Any authenticated user can read any invoice (IDOR in get_invoice)

evidence.content: cart = db().execute("SELECT id, total FROM carts WHERE user_id = ?", (current_user().id,)).fetchone()

findings.description: get_invoice looks up an invoice solely by the client-supplied id. owner_id is fetched and even returned, but never compared to the session user. Elsewhere (apply_coupon) the code scopes queries by current_user().id, showing the intended ownership pattern.
findings.attack_scenario: A logged-in user changes the numeric id in /invoices/<id> to another customer's invoice id and receives that invoice's owner and total. (Not executed.)
findings.expected_boundary: A user can read only invoices where owner_id equals their user id.
findings.observed_behavior: Query filters by id only; no owner comparison on any path in the handler.
findings.technical_impact: Horizontal disclosure of all customers' invoice data (owner id, totals).

verification.rationale: get_invoice is reachable by any session (login_required only), selects by id alone and never compares owner_id; no before_request hook, middleware or DB policy in the snapshot adds an ownership check.

findings.safe_validation: Static: confirm no middleware or DB row-level policy enforces ownership; optionally write a unit test against a local throwaway DB fixture (never production).
findings.remediation: Filter by owner: WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ? with current_user().id, or check row[1] == current_user().id and return 404 otherwise.

findings.title: Single-use coupon is never enforced and discounts compound on repeat calls

evidence.content:
coupon = db().execute("SELECT percent, single_use FROM coupons WHERE code = ?", (code,)).fetchone()
new_total = cart[1] * (100 - coupon[0]) / 100
db().execute("UPDATE carts SET total = ? WHERE id = ?", (new_total, cart[0]))

findings.description: apply_coupon selects single_use but never checks or records redemption, and applies the percentage to the already-discounted cart total. Repeating the request reduces the total geometrically toward zero.
findings.attack_scenario: Calling /cart/apply-coupon N times with a 20% code reduces the total to 0.8^N of the original. (Not executed.)
findings.expected_boundary: A single-use coupon reduces one order once.
findings.observed_behavior: No redemption record; discount re-applied on each call.
findings.technical_impact: Fraudulent discounts / goods obtained below price.

verification.rationale: single_use is selected but never read; the total is re-discounted on every call. Unproven: whether a DB trigger elsewhere limits redemptions.
missing_prerequisites: Database schema/triggers for coupons are not in the snapshot

findings.safe_validation: Static trace of apply_coupon; local unit test on a throwaway DB calling the handler twice.
findings.remediation: Record redemptions (unique constraint on coupon+user/order), enforce single_use, compute discounts from the undiscounted subtotal, make the operation idempotent.

history.note: severity high -> medium to match CVSS 6.5
